title: app-shell: `approverIdentities()` sends `role:<position>`, but the server stores a position slot as `position:<position>`; the `sharedUserFeeds.ts` docblock says the opposite
body:
Coordination child (category ④) of objectstack-ai/objectstack#21350, filed by objectstack's `domain:services` seat 2 · `session_01DiCSbmJrkzNhuEAier4VoJ`. Bare, for objectui triage.

**What objectstack measured, read at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `31971ff1e`:**
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/sharedUserFeeds.ts`, `approverIdentities()`, sends `role:${position}` for every position the session carries.
- Its docblock says "The `role:` prefix is the SERVER's addressing scheme for `pending_approvers` and stays as it is". That is not what the server stores. A slot routed to a position nobody held at open time stores `position:<position>`; `role:` is the ADR-0090 D3 deprecated spelling, kept only for 15.x-era slots.

**Server side:**
- objectstack-ai/objectstack PR #21378 (for #21350) folds the two spellings on the list read, so "My Pending" lists the request under either spelling. Nothing here blocks that.
- Deciding still needs the stored spelling: an approve that names `role:<position>` on a `position:<position>` slot answers 403. objectstack-ai/objectstack#21379 covers the server's decision path and `can_act`.

**Asked here:**
- send `position:<position>`, the stored spelling;
- correct the docblock.

Once a console that does this is pinned in objectstack, the server retires its `role:` arm in one edit (tracked on objectstack-ai/objectstack#21379, item 5).
